labels.text: Add custom instructions here.
Custom instructions:

S85.02.note: The CLI reads this file from the home folder and from .agiworkforce/instructions.md in a project; the account-level instructions are edited only on the web page the CLI links to.
steps: In Terminal, run "agi init" (it creates ~/.agiworkforce/instructions.md if it is missing).
Open ~/.agiworkforce/instructions.md and add a line under the heading, for example "Always answer in one sentence." Save the file.
Run "agi", ask a simple question, and check that the reply follows the line.
Remove the line, save, start a new chat, ask the same question, and check the reply no longer follows it.
S85.02.where: Terminal: run "agi init", then open ~/.agiworkforce/instructions.md in a text editor. Account-level custom instructions are not in the CLI: "/personalize show" prints a web link to Settings > General.

labels.text: Response style
Usage: /personalize [show]
Personalization (your AGI account):

S85.03.needs: a signed-in AGI account (Managed Cloud mode)
S85.03.note: The code says these settings apply to Managed Cloud chats only, not Local or BYOK sessions, which is narrower than "on the surface".
steps: Start "agi" and type "/personalize show"; look for the line "Response style" with the value not set.
Type "/personalize set style concise"; look for "Response style set to concise."
Type "/personalize set length shorter"; look for "Length set to shorter."
Ask a question such as "What is a closure?" and compare the reply's tone, length and formatting with Expected.
S85.03.where: In an agi session, type "/personalize show", then "/personalize set style concise" (other fields: length, formatting, warmth, enthusiasm, headings, emoji).

labels.text: Turn account memory on, so details are carried across conversations on every surface.
Memory is off for your account. Turn it on with `agi memory on`.
Your AGI account holds no memories in

S85.05.needs: a signed-in AGI account (Managed Cloud mode)
S85.05.note: The in-app "/memory" command manages local memory files on this computer, not the saved account memories that "agi memory" manages.
steps: Run "agi memory status"; look for "Memory is on:" or "Memory is off:".
Run "agi memory add Prefers short answers", then "agi memory list"; look for the new memory in the list.
Run "agi memory edit <id or text> Prefers detailed answers", then "agi memory list" to see the new text.
Run "agi memory forget <id or text>", then "agi memory list"; the memory should be gone.
Run "agi memory off", start a chat, and compare with Expected: memories should not be used while memory is off.
S85.05.where: Terminal: "agi memory" with the subcommands list, add, edit, forget, on, off, status ("agi memory list" shows saved memories).

labels.text: Keep session history:
Usage: /config [show|get <key>|set <key> <value>]

S85.11.note: The code turns off session saving on this computer; the code does not show that the choice is synced to the account, so that part of Expected is unverified.
steps: Type "/config get history"; look for "history = true" or "Unknown or unset key: 'history'" if it was never set.
Type "/config set history false"; look for "history = false (saved)".
Start a new chat, send one message, quit, then run "agi history" in Terminal and check whether the new chat is listed.
Run "agi --config"; look for "Keep session history: false" and compare with Expected.
S85.11.where: In an agi session, type "/config set history false" (alias: "/config set keep-history false"). Check with "/config get history" and "agi --config".

labels.text: Usage: /config set <key> <value>
Usage: /config [show|get <key>|set <key> <value>]

S85.14.needs: none to change the setting; a Managed Cloud account for reports to be sent
S85.14.note: Crash reports send only in Managed mode, and the AGI_CRASH_REPORTS environment variable overrides the saved choice; no on-screen confirmation of an upload was found.
steps: Type "/config get crash-reports"; look for "crash-reports = false", the default.
Type "/config set crash-reports true"; look for "crash-reports = true (saved)".
Type "/config get crash-reports" again and confirm the value is true; then set it back to false.
Type "/config set product-analytics false" and check with "/config get product-analytics"; compare with Expected.
S85.14.where: In an agi session, type "/config set crash-reports true" (or false) and "/config set product-analytics false". Read back with "/config get crash-reports".

S85.16.note: Searched apps/cli/src for temporary, incognito and temp-chat controls: found only help text about temporary chats in apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs and the per-run --no-session-persistence flag, with no by-default setting; the nearest control is "/config set history false" (S85.11), which does not mention memory.

labels.text: Archived sessions (agi session unarchive <id> restores one):
Archive a session (hidden from active listings, kept on disk).
No archived sessions. `agi session archive <id>` archives one.

S85.17.needs: a saved session on this computer
S85.17.note: These commands cover sessions saved on this computer; no CLI command was found to list or restore archived cloud chats ("agi history delete <id>" only deletes a cloud conversation).
steps: Run "agi session list" and note the id of one session.
Run "agi session archive <id>", then "agi session list"; the session should no longer appear in the active list.
Run "agi session list --archived"; look for "Archived sessions (agi session unarchive <id> restores one):" with the session in it.
Run "agi session unarchive <id>"; look for "Unarchived" and check the session is back in "agi session list".
Run "agi session delete <id>" and answer the confirmation; compare with Expected (the help text says it is permanent).
S85.17.where: Terminal: "agi session list", "agi session list --archived", "agi session archive <id>", "agi session unarchive <id>", "agi session delete <id>".

labels.text: Shared conversation links
agi shares revoke <token> turns a link off for everyone.

S85.19.needs: a signed-in AGI account with at least one shared chat link
S85.19.note: The CLI lists only chat share links; no CLI listing of shared published pages was found, and the code warns the list may be incomplete.
steps: Run "agi shares"; look for "Shared conversation links" and the token of each link.
Run "agi shares revoke <token>" and answer the confirmation (or add -y).
Run "agi shares" again; the revoked link should be gone.
Open the revoked link's address in a private browser window and check it no longer opens.
S85.19.where: Terminal: "agi shares" to list links and "agi shares revoke <token>" to turn one off.

labels.text: Export your account data: request an export, or download the one that is ready.
Your export is ready. Run `agi export-data` again to download it.

S85.20.needs: a signed-in AGI account; the export can take a while to prepare
S85.20.note: The CLI code downloads the archive but does not show its contents, so whether it includes all four kinds of data is unverified.
steps: Run "agi export-data"; the first run requests the export and reports that it is being prepared.
Wait, then run "agi export-data" again; look for "Your export is ready. Run `agi export-data` again to download it."
Run "agi export-data" once more; look for "Saved" followed by the file path.
Open the saved file and check it holds chats, memory, files and settings, comparing with Expected.

labels.text: Import memories from a text or markdown file, such as another assistant's export.
Nothing new to import: every memory in that file is already in your account.

S85.22.needs: a signed-in AGI account and a text or markdown file with memories
S85.22.note: The CLI sends the file to the server for a preview and then a commit; how the server splits the file into single memories is not in the CLI code.
steps: Create a plain text file of memories in your own words, for example memories.txt on the Desktop.
Run "agi memory import ~/Desktop/memories.txt --source "Other assistant""; look for the line that starts "Imported" and reports the count.
Run "agi memory list" and find the imported memories.
Run the same import command again; look for "Nothing new to import: every memory in that file is already in your account."
S85.22.where: Terminal: "agi memory import <file>" with an optional "--source <name>" (the default source is Other).
